lessons: Contradicts the guide: my WR with no flexible late threat won 2-0 in 24- and 21-turn games and again in 20- and 28-turn games, so long games were not automatically lost.
I lost 1-2 to WR seat 4 with two Thraben Sentry, two Selfless Cathar and two Unruly Mob but only three fliers; take a third flier over a second Unruly Mob.
Seat 4's WR went 3-0 on Rebuke, Rally the Peasants, Furor of the Bitten and Voiceless Spirit, so take those early and trust the guide's fast WR line.
Draft answers to flyers early: I lost 0-2 to WR with two Abbey Griffin and 1-2 to WU with Angel of Flight Alabaster; my only reach was Geistflame and Brimstone Volley.
Smite the Monstrous hits power four or more, so my Morkrut Banshee and Falkenrath Noble top end was exposed; draft cheaper threats below power four so one removal spell can't blank the curve.
I cut Cobbled Wings for the ground creature base, leaving no way for my Devils and Werewolves to get past white flying blockers.
The guide calls WU the strongest common archetype, but my WU went 4-4 in games and lost 0-2 to WR in a 28-turn grind. Draft more cheap evasive threats, not Think Twice filler.
Ghoulcaller's Bell at pick 14 was a wasted pick; the guide's skip list was right, so take playable creatures over marginal late picks.
Opposing WR ran Rebuke, Fiend Hunter, Slayer of the Wicked and Bonds of Faith; take instant-speed answers like Smite the Monstrous before marginal creatures to clear blockers.
My UB deck went 0-3 (3-6 in games) with 13 to 28 turn games, so prioritise a low curve and early creatures over marginal fliers like Cobbled Wings and Trepanation Blade.
In pack 2 I took Spectral Flight and Moon Heron twice each; a second copy of an evasion spell cost me a playable creature for the curve.
I ran 17 lands with 10 Swamp and 7 Island and still lost every round 1-2, so check colour sources and threat count before settling on a 23-spell list.

Tonight contradicted the guide: a WR with only one flier (Voiceless Spirit) went 3-0 by curving out with Ashmouth Hound, Thraben Sentry, Elder Cathar, Furor of the Bitten, Rebuke and Into the Maw of Hell.
Cutting green, Traitorous Blood and Curse of the Pierced Heart for a clean two-colour WR core worked; splashing or hedging would have diluted the curve and removal.
Red and white flowed through picks 4-8 of packs 2 and 3 (Pitchburn Devils, Rage Thrower, Rebuke, Bonds of Faith), so commit to the open pair early instead of hedging.
Stalled WU shells lose long games: my fliers and Sensory Deprivation and Claustrophobia could not close the 26- and 24-turn losses to WG, so favor a faster curve and early pressure.
Seat 4's WR went 3-0 and beat my WU 2-1 with Furor of the Bitten and Pitchburn Devils, so stay open to red-white aggression rather than committing early to blue.
The second Moment of Heroism (pack 1, pick 11) was cut before play, so take a playable creature over a redundant combat trick once your deck already has one.
Take evasion over ground filler: my WG deck's only fliers were Chapel Geist and Voiceless Spirit, and the 37-turn loss to BG's ground board showed that fliers win, as the guide says.
Take cheap interaction before ground bodies: Blazing Torch and Feeling of Dread were my only cheap answers, which left me short against UB's Moon Herons and BG's Garruk Relentless.
Take cheap two-drops and cheap interaction over a fourth top-end fatty: our BG games ran 16 to 37 turns, and we went 4-5 in games, losing to WU fliers and WR tricks.
Expect WU's Stitched Drakes and Murder of Crows and WR's Pitchburn Devils; our BG answers were mainly Victim of Night, Prey Upon and Corpse Lunge, so draft reach or flier removal earlier.
